findings.title: Arch boundary has no slice, so its index and status carrier are unspecified
findings.description:
The slice says `deriveSliceStatus()` sets `pending-review`/`review-failed` and that `getNext()` maps those statuses to recommendations. The `arch` boundary ("arch exists, no slice plan") has no slice, so `SliceStatus` has nothing to attach to. The doc says only that the "no-active-slice / pre-slice-plan path" is extended.
- It does not say which index is passed to `detectDocuments(path, index, 'arch')`. The arch review is named by the arch index, not a slice index.
- It does not say how a per-slice status reaches the `review-gate` branch when no slice exists.
- It does not say how this path is distinguished from the other no-active-slice states.
- The architecture defers this boundary as "a later slice", and the slice plan folded it into 241. 241 therefore has to define the mechanism, and today it only asserts "one more case of the single mechanism". State the index source and the status or recommendation carrier for this boundary.

findings.title: Evaluator and config-resolution contracts contradict each other
findings.description:
- Config reading is described two ways. "Config Injection" says the navigator owns resolution, calling `this.config?.get(...)` and handing raw values to `reviewGate` (line 109). TD-1 and the data flow have `resolveGateConfig(config)` inside `reviewGate.ts` taking the `ConfigManager`. The same section rejects "resolving config inside the navigator" as coupling core to config I/O.
- `evaluateVerdict` is declared to return `clears`/`pending`/`failed`, but TD-2 says the navigator supplies `pending` from `review === null`. The function therefore never returns `pending`, and the `GateOutcome` type is wider than the function's real range.
- Slice 242 needs the same absent / present-failing / clears distinction. It must emit a `warning` for a missing artifact and an `error` for a failing verdict. If `pending` lives in the navigator, 242 either re-derives it or imports navigator logic. That defeats the stated reason for a standalone module.
- Fix: pick one owner for config reading, and make the shared evaluator take an artifact-or-null so it returns all three outcomes.

findings.title: Failure modes for the review-file read are not observable, and one architecture requirement can't be met
findings.description:
- The architecture requires that for an unparseable review file "the rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." The slice relies on `parseFrontmatter` returning `{found:false, data:{}}` for every read or parse error. A read failure, malformed YAML and a missing `verdict` are therefore indistinguishable, so the rationale can't name a parse failure. TD-7 requires only the review type, and the verdict and threshold for `review-failed`.
- No signal is specified for these cases. The navigator's existing warnings pattern could carry it, and nothing says it will be used. Project rules require every failure mode to be observable (WARNING+ or a metric), with a test asserting that signal.
- Nothing covers invalid config values. This includes a non-boolean `review_enabled`, an invalid per-gate threshold, and `ConfigManager.get` throwing on a malformed TOML file. The architecture says these fail fast through the `validate` hook, and the slice says "narrow explicitly" but not what happens when narrowing fails. A silent fall-through to gating-off would violate "never use silent fallback values."
- Fix: separate read failure from absent verdict, attach a warning to the `NextAction`, and enumerate the config-error behavior with a test for each.

findings.title: Per-gate `review_type` keys are left defined but silently ignored
findings.description:
TD-4 keeps `workflow.review_gates.{gate}.review_type` as keys that are "defined but unread".
- A user who sets one gets no error and no effect. The architecture's "fail-fast on configuration errors" principle exists to prevent that.
- The slice plan allows either "leave inert" or "241 removes them", and 241 is the slice that must decide. The doc defers the decision with "flagged for the PM at implementation".
- Inert config is also a surface that nothing uses. The documentation obligation is pushed to 243 only to explain keys that shouldn't exist.
- Either remove the keys now, or reject non-empty values with a clear error.
- Also state how the camelCase `Boundary` values (`preAdvance`, etc.) map to the architecture's kebab-case config gate names (`pre-advance`). That mapping is a second set of comparison values and is not defined once.

findings.title: Evaluation scope and retroactivity are not defined
findings.description:
The slice says the gate is folded into `deriveSliceStatus()` "so the new statuses flow through `getStatus()` to every consumer".
- It does not say whether the gate runs for every slice or only the active one. If it runs for every slice, enabling gating on an existing project turns every historically `complete` slice with no code review into `pending-review`. That adds a filesystem read per slice per call.
- A slice already in implementation, with no tasks review on disk, regresses from `in-implementation` to `pending-review`.
- The architecture requires that an ungated project sees no change. It does not address enabling gating on a project already in flight, and the slice needs to say which behavior it intends.
- State the evaluated set (active slice only, or gated by the plan's checked state) and how mid-flight slices are treated.

findings.title: Design is heavier than needed and repeats itself
findings.description:
Cut or merge the following:
- The lifecycle table (lines 20-28) and the "Boundary → signal" table (130-141) cover the same four boundaries. Merge them into one table.
- Drop the "Retired by this slice's model" paragraph. It restates the slice plan's note on slice 244.
- Drop `positionToReviewType()`. It is a one-line wrapper over `BOUNDARY_REVIEW_TYPE[boundary]`, and callers can index the constant directly.
- Cut "Rejected alternatives" down to one line, or drop it. The decision is already stated.
- "Component Structure", "Provides to Other Slices" and "Deferred to Other Slices" restate the Technical Scope and the slice plan.
- The eight-step walkthrough could be trimmed to roughly four steps. Gating off, pre-advance pending, pre-advance failed, and a threshold change cover every distinct behavior.

The `STATUS` const is assigned to 241 by the slice plan, and keeping the 50-site sweep in 910 is a sound call.

findings.title: Deviations from the architecture are deliberate and consistent with the slice plan
findings.description:
- Position-derived review type replaces the architecture's configurable `reviewType`, as the slice plan's Phase 4 note records.
- The `pre-slice-plan` gate is folded into 241 rather than left to a separate slice, and slice 244 is retired.
- `UNKNOWN` is never mapped to `pending-review`. The architecture allowed it, and the slice's reasoning (an existing file is never "not yet reviewed") is sound.
- `score` is not read at all. The architecture said it should be read and stored but not enforced. This is harmless in v1, but 242 or a later slice will need to add the read.
- The worktree-scope claim ("inherited for free") is plausible for the CLI. The two MCP call sites are not shown to resolve a worktree-aware path, and no success criterion tests worktree scope. The architecture's related work says `review_*` keys should resolve at worktree scope.

findings.title: Conservative default, dependency direction and recommendation vocabulary are sound
findings.description:
- The optional constructor dependency makes the "no config or `review_enabled` false means identical behavior" guarantee structural. A dedicated regression test is required to verify it.
- `reviewGate.ts` sits beside the navigator and does not import it, so 242 can depend on the evaluator without a cycle.
- CF routes to a review and does not perform or advance one, which matches the architecture's layer boundaries. The `code` trigger is checkbox completion, so CF does not inspect git.
- The `NextAction` type is unchanged and only new `recommendation` strings are added, which keeps the Amoeba contract stable.
- The verdict and threshold decision matrix is explicit and covers the `review_unknown_as` interaction the architecture calls out.

structured_findings.summary: Arch boundary has no slice, so its index and status carrier are unspecified
Evaluator and config-resolution contracts contradict each other
Failure modes for the review-file read are not observable, and one architecture requirement can't be met
Per-gate `review_type` keys are left defined but silently ignored
Evaluation scope and retroactivity are not defined
Design is heavier than needed and repeats itself
Deviations from the architecture are deliberate and consistent with the slice plan
Conservative default, dependency direction and recommendation vocabulary are sound
